record.original_question: The Fatou Set of a Polynomial Automorphism of C^2 . Let f be a polynomial automorphism of C^2 , and suppose that f is not conjugate to an elementary map. Let Omega be a connected component of the set of points where the forward iterates {f n : n = 1, 2, 3, ...} are locally bounded, which is the Fatou set of f . Let us suppose that Omega is periodic, i.e. f n Omega = Omega for some n 6= 0. Let us first consider the case in which Omega is recurrent, i.e. Omega contains a point whose orbit does not converge to ∂Omega. In this case Omega is either (a) a basin of attraction of a sink orbit, (b) the basin of attractin of a Siegel disk, or (c) the basin of a Herman ring. It is not hard to construct examples of (a) and (b). (i) Can case (c) occur? Nothing at all seems to be known about periodic domains which are not recurrent. (ii) If Omega is not recurrent, does there exist P ∈ ∂Omega such that limk→∞ f nk (Q) = P for all Q ∈ Omega? (iii) If Omega is not recurrent, does there exist P ∈ ∂Omega such that f n P = P , and one of the eigenvalues of DF (P ) is e2πip/q ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f be a polynomial automorphism of C^2 that is not conjugate to an elementary map (i.e., it has nontrivial dynamics; equivalently, after conjugation by polynomial automorphisms, it is a finite composition of generalized Hénon maps). Define the Fatou set of f to be the set of points p ∈ C^2 having a neighborhood on which the family of forward iterates {f^n : n = 1, 2, 3, …} is locally bounded (equivalently, locally equicontinuous on compact sets). Let Ω be a connected component of the Fatou set and suppose Ω is periodic, meaning f^n(Ω) = Ω for some integer n ≠ 0. Call Ω recurrent if it contains a point whose forward orbit does not converge to ∂Ω.

It is known that if Ω is periodic and recurrent, then Ω is one of:
(a) the basin of attraction of an attracting periodic orbit (sink),
(b) the basin of a Siegel disk (periodic point with both eigenvalues of modulus 1, conjugate to a rotation), or
(c) the basin of a Herman ring (an invariant annulus on which the dynamics is conjugate to an irrational rotation).

Examples are known for cases (a) and (b). Resolve the following:

(i) Can case (c) occur? That is, does there exist a polynomial automorphism of C^2 (non-elementary) possessing a periodic recurrent Fatou component which is the basin of a Herman ring?

(ii) Suppose Ω is a periodic Fatou component that is not recurrent. Must there exist a point P ∈ ∂Ω such that, for every Q ∈ Ω, lim_{k→∞} f^{nk}(Q) = P (along the period-n iterates)?

(iii) Under the same hypothesis (Ω periodic, non-recurrent), must there exist a point P ∈ ∂Ω with f^n(P) = P such that one of the eigenvalues of Df^n(P) equals e^{2πi p/q} for some rational p/q?
artifact.status_search_result: Part (i) (existence of Herman rings) was a long-standing open problem; a 2025 preprint by Krikorian announces the existence of Herman rings (and "exotic rotation domains") for quadratic Hénon maps, which if confirmed resolves (i) affirmatively. Parts (ii) and (iii), concerning non-recurrent periodic Fatou components, appear to remain open: very little is known about non-recurrent periodic Fatou components for polynomial automorphisms of C^2, although related progress on wandering Fatou components (Astorg–Boc Thaler–Peters and others) has been made.

status_evidence.snippet: Existence of polynomial automorphisms of C^2 with wandering Fatou components.
